transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-11-03
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Tariq Ahmed (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Liam Ortega (Halcyon VP Eng), Priya Nair (Halcyon SRE Lead), Zoe Kim (Halcyon PM)

Summary (auto): Brief recap of outage on 2028-10-29, agreed triage, scheduled shadow run and sprint.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Emily: ok folks, thanks for joining, we're going to keep this tight, we've got 50 minutes but plenty to cover. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Liam: Liam here.
[00:09] Priya: Priya on the call.
[00:11] Zoe: Zoe here.
[00:12] Emily: Tara— sorry Tariq and Maya from Redwood?
[00:14] Tariq: Tariq speaking, SE, hi.
[00:15] Maya: Maya here.
[00:17] Emily: Cool. So goal, recap root cause and agree remediation / preventive sprint. Priya, do you want to give the customer view of impact?
[00:26] Priya: Yeah so on 10/29 at around 13:10 UTC we saw a cascade of 503s for our routing service. Latency climbed, tokens queued... users saw failed shipments creation which is, uh, revenue-impacting. Our initial signal was a backlog in requests hitting the Redwood inference endpoint — we use Redwood Dedicated for some high-throughput routes — and then we saw continuous kv eviction spikes which made tail latency blow out.
[00:50] Tariq: (soft) eviction... kv cache eviction spike hmm. Can you share the metric that shows the working set growth, was it sequence length related or simply throughput?
[00:58] Priya: It looks related to both. During a promo we had longer sequences, more context, and then downstream retry logic amplified the pressure. Also our autoscaler kicked in late — we had a scale-up delay of about 2 minutes.
[01:14] Emily: ok that's super helpful. From Redwood's end our logs show many small bursts of repeated identical prefixes — prefix cache hit rate dropped from 78% to 21% during the window. We also saw lots of concurrent KV writes that increased mem pressure. Sorry sometimes our transcribe, it reads "kv" as K V or like key-vee, so just to clarify.
[01:35] Liam: Right, we saw retries from the worker pool — it doesn't respect jitter well.
[01:38] Zoe: can we pause — when you say prefix cache drop, is that because of TTL mismatches or because new model variant changed tokenization?
[01:45] Tariq: Good question. Our hypothesis is eviction due to working set explosion + quantized model shard boundary behavior. There was also a small mismatch: you had pinned a model at v1.3 but some routes were using v1.3-quant which changes kv key shapes slightly. That decreased hit overlap.
[02:05] Priya: hmm we did roll a new variant on 10/27 but we thought it was backward compatible.
[02:09] Maya: Ok so the RCA we trust is multi-factor: working set growth from longer prompts, variant mismatch reducing cache sharing, and autoscaler thresholds being conservative so scale lagged. On the call today we want to agree short-term mitigations and a preventive sprint.
[02:26] Emily: Right. Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) tighten retry backoff on your side (reduce immediate retries), 2) enable prefix-only caching for the hot routes to protect KV from thrash, and 3) temporary increase Dedicated pool headroom to absorb bursts. We'd also run a 48-hour shadow test on Redwood Dedicated with your production traffic to validate.
[02:47] Liam: The headroom bump is fine short-term, but cost is a concern. What will that look like cost-wise?
[02:53] Emily: We'll send an estimated delta after this call — worst-case a 20% bump in reserved if you want guaranteed capacity, or we can do a timed burst allocation for the pilot which is lower.
[03:03] Zoe: and what about the autoscaler tuning?
[03:06] Tariq: We propose two changes: adjust scale-up to be more aggressive (threshold from 80% to 65% CPU/queue) and shorten cooldown from 120s to 45s for the routes with high SLA. Also add a pre-warming policy based on predictive traffic — we can use your calendar/promos signals.
[03:24] Priya: predictive pre-warming sounds great but we need the ability to opt-out for certain noisy campaigns.
[03:29] Emily: Of course, opt-out toggles will be in the pilot config.
[03:32] Zoe: One ask — can Redwood surface a specific runbook for how to flip these toggles and rollback? We had some confusion during the incident.
[03:41] Maya: Yes, we have runbook templates. I'll share a diff showing recommended changes; it will include rollback steps and a checklist.
[03:48] Liam: Also we need audit logs and SOC2 evidence — we need to show internal auditors the controls for key rotation and access to logs.
[03:55] Emily: We can share the SOC2 artifact bundle and the KMS integration doc. Note that for Private deployments there's additional artifact detail, but we'll share what we can for Dedicated.
[04:05] Priya: Great. Back to technicals — Tariq, you mentioned model variant causing keyshape differences. Could you explain that so our ML folks understand?
[04:12] Tariq: Sure, in brief: the quantized variant uses a slightly different token merge behavior and that changed prefix normalization. So previously multiple prompts would map to the same prefix key; with the quantized variant they diverged leading to less sharing in the prefix space. It's subtle but it compounds when sequences are long.
[04:30] Zoe: so solution is to standardize on a single variant for those routes?
[04:33] Tariq: Either standardize or use deterministic normalization step before sending. We can push a middleware shim to normalize tokens client-side, or we can roll back the variant until cache hit rates stabilize. For the sprint we recommend normalizing and running the shadow test.
[04:46] Priya: ok. On retries: we currently do immediate retries x3 within 10s window. We'll add jitter and exponential backoff.
[04:54] Liam: We also discovered some client code that didn't close streams cleanly which held KV references longer. Small bug but amplified during the event. We'll ship a fix this week.
[05:03] Maya: Good call, small fixes matter.
[05:06] Emily: Quick logistics: we propose a 3-week preventive sprint starting 2028-11-12 with the following milestones — week 1: runbook + quick fixes + shadow config; week 2: 48-hour shadow run and observability validation; week 3: rollout of autoscaler tune and production cutover. Does that timeline work?
[05:24] Priya: Tight but doable. We need to align product and SRE calendars.
[05:28] Zoe: Also we want to include a post-sprint evaluation that measures tail latency P95/99 and cost delta.
[05:33] Tariq: We'll provide dashboards and a comparison spreadsheet. We'll also include a regression test harness to validate output quality after any quantization or variant changes.
[05:43] Liam: On the regression harness, please ensure we capture prompt-level goldens. We had a subtle quality drift on a high-value route last quarter.
[05:52] Emily: Absolutely, Redwood Optimize recommendations will run evals against your deck and we'll highlight any regressions. We'll also wire up alerting to your SLO channel if quality delta exceeds threshold.
[06:02] Priya: A question about observability — during the incident some spans were missing. Is that on our side or Redwood's tracing?
[06:08] Tariq: From our trace logs some sidecar spans failed because of sampling config. We'll collaborate to ensure 100% sampling for the pilot window and then toggle to adaptive sampling after.
[06:19] Zoe: Do you have a checklist for required instrumentation?
[06:22] Maya: Yes I'll include an instrumentation checklist: request IDs, trace IDs, cache hit metrics, eviction counters, queue depth, and tokenization hash metrics.
[06:31] Priya: Thanks. Ok can we go over the shadow test plan briefly?
[06:35] Tariq: Plan high-level: mirror production traffic to a Dedicated shadow pool with same model variant + normalized prefixing. No writes to downstream systems — just simulate inference calls and measure latency, hit rates, and eviction behavior. We'll run 48 hours and compare to baseline. Metrics to capture: prefix_hit_rate, kv_eviction_rate, p95/p99 latency, queue depth, scale events. We'll also capture quantization output diffs.
[07:03] Liam: Sounds reasonable. For the shadow pool do we need to provision immediately?
[07:07] Emily: We can provision a temporary Dedicated pool for the test window. Cost estimate will be in spreadsheet. Optionally use burst capacity if you'd prefer ephemeral.
[07:16] Priya: We'll review costs, but pilot is priority.
[07:19] Zoe: One more security note — the shadow pool will still see PII in prompts; we need to ensure logs are masked and retention is limited.
[07:27] Tariq: Right, we'll apply redaction rules and limit retention to 7 days for the pilot. Also encrypt logs at rest using your KMS if integrated.
[07:36] Emily: Ok quick check: middleware normalization shim — who's owning dev work?
[07:41] Liam: Our infra team can own the shim, but Redwood can provide the tokenizer normalization snippet.
[07:46] Tariq: We'll deliver a reference lib in Python and Node and some example unit tests.
[07:52] Priya: That helps.
[07:55] Emily: Moving toward a close: let's recap commitments — Emily to send plan and cost; Tariq to send diagnostic script and token normalization lib; Maya to send runbook template and instrumentation checklist; Priya to provide logs and confirm pilot window. Anything else?
[08:11] Zoe: Please also include a short FAQ for our execs describing risk tradeoffs: cost vs latency, dedicated vs hosted.
[08:18] Emily: We'll include a one-pager.
[08:20] Liam: Competitor question — NimbusAI reached out offering caching add-ons, should we evaluate?
[08:24] Emily: We know them — they do caching but they don't have our unified fallback routing or quantization-aware kernels. We'll share a comparison but focus on stabilizing first.
[08:35] Priya: Ok fine.
[08:36] Maya: Scheduling: shall we lock the shadow run 2028-11-09 to 2028-11-11?
[08:40] Priya: That works if we can get logs to you by 11/5.
[08:43] Emily: We'll treat that as tentative until we get Priya's exports.
[08:46] Zoe: Anything else on telemetry?
[08:48] Tariq: We'll add a short healthcheck endpoint for the pilot that surfaces cache metrics in plain JSON so your ops can poll.
[08:55] Liam: Good.
[08:57] Emily: Ok closing notes — next sync after the shadow run kickoff will be 2028-11-10 quick status check, then post-run debrief 2028-11-13. We'll send invites.
[09:09] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[09:11] Emily: Thanks, meeting adjourned.

--- End Transcript ---
